decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding agree that the paper is a replication study using a new sample from the Building Strong Families dataset to re-test Volling et al. (2019).

decisions.quote:
Interestingly, we found that the proportion of fathers with a
supportive parenting profile (55.21%) was greater than that of
mothers with a supportive parenting profile (25.91%). This seems
inconsistent with previous research, which found that middle-class
(Volling et al., 2019) and low-income (Ryan et al., 2006) mothers
were more likely than their counterpart fathers to be characterized
by supportive parenting.
decisions.reason: While the emergence of an activation parenting profile for fathers and mothers replicated Volling et al. (2019), the authors also explicitly hypothesized based on Volling et al. (2019) that the activation profile would describe more fathers than mothers, and they explicitly mark their resulting mother/father profile proportions and family configurations as differing from and inconsistent with Volling et al. (2019). The conclusion only confirms that key findings were replicated 'in this regard' (the emergence of the activation profile), rather than stating an unqualified overall verdict overriding the explicit contrast.
